title: Refactor Go web app: extract ItemStore interface, inject into Server struct
description: The Go web app uses package-level mutable state and hard-coded template paths. Refactor to a Server struct that accepts an ItemStore interface and a template directory path, making it testable without real files.

task_spec.prompt:
The Go web app in internal/handler/items.go uses a package-level Store slice and a templateDir() helper that resolves paths via runtime.Caller. Refactor WITHOUT changing any HTTP routes or response shapes:

1. Define type ItemStore interface { All() []Item; Filter(q string) []Item } in internal/handler/store.go.
2. Define type InMemoryStore struct { items []Item } implementing ItemStore. Move Store initialization into InMemoryStore. Add NewInMemoryStore(items []Item) *InMemoryStore constructor.
3. Define type Server struct { store ItemStore; tmplDir string } with methods ServeIndex, ServeAPIItems that replace Index and APIItems. The Server uses s.tmplDir to load templates (not runtime.Caller).
4. Update cmd/server/main.go to construct Server with NewInMemoryStore(defaultItems) and a tmplDir resolved at startup.
5. Rewrite items_test.go to test through Server with an InMemoryStore seeded inline — no package-level ResetStore() needed.

All existing HTTP behaviour (routes, response shapes, filter behaviour) must be identical. go test ./... must pass. go vet ./... must be clean.
required_artifacts: internal/handler/store.go with ItemStore interface and InMemoryStore
Server struct with ServeIndex and ServeAPIItems methods
Tests rewritten to construct Server with injected store
success_criteria: ItemStore interface enables mock injection in tests
Server struct holds no global mutable state
HTTP surface unchanged (same routes, same JSON shapes)
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `go test ./...` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
